stem.text: Meselson and Stahl investigated DNA replication by growing bacteria in a culture containing heavy nitrogen, ${}^{15}\text{N}$, until all the DNA was labelled.
These bacteria, the parental generation, were then transferred to a culture containing only light nitrogen, ${}^{14}\text{N}$, and allowed to replicate for two generations.
DNA was extracted from each generation of bacteria and its relative mass estimated. The flow diagram shows the results.

stem.alt: Flow diagram with three stages in a vertical sequence, with a column of relative mass of DNA values on the right: 100% heavy, 100% medium, then 50% medium and 50% light after the second generation.
